reports.title: Suncor Energy reports third quarter 2026 results

desk.headline: Record cash flow; adjusted EPS C$3.97 vs C$1.48, beat; 2026 guidance unchanged, dividend up 10% and buybacks raised
results: Adjusted operating earnings rose to C$4.6bn (C$3.97 a share) from C$1.8bn on higher oil prices, much stronger refining margins and more exports.
Reported net earnings were C$3.8bn, after a C$1.1bn write-down on offshore assets being sold.
Record adjusted funds from operations of C$6.7bn; free funds flow was C$5.2bn and net debt fell to C$1.75bn.
Upstream output slipped 2% to 852,500 bbl/d on Syncrude maintenance; refined product sales hit a Q3 record of 677,000 bbl/d.
C$2.0bn returned in the quarter; since then the dividend rose 10% to C$0.66 and monthly buybacks went to C$750m from C$500m.

guidance.summary: Suncor says its 2026 guidance ranges (last updated 4 Aug 2026) are unchanged. It now expects about C$5.5bn of share buybacks for 2026.

items.new: About C$5.5bn (C$750m a month from Oct)

points: CEO Rich Kruger said refined product exports are up about 80% this year, to 75,000 bbl/d, reaching the US West Coast, Scandinavia, Iceland and Central America.
Nine chartered ships are giving big savings against spot freight rates; Kruger expects that benefit to last well into next year.
Management said Suncor is keeping its non-operated Hebron and Hibernia stakes after agreeing to sell Terra Nova and White Rose to Ithaca for C$1.2bn.
Coverage noted higher freight costs have widened the discount on Canadian heavy oil.
call.source: Call coverage: The Canadian Press via BNN Bloomberg, 4 Nov 2026; Reuters via Offshore Engineer, 4 Nov 2026

watch: Whether refining margins and export volumes stay this strong into Q4.
Closing of the offshore asset sale, expected early 2027.
Buybacks running at C$750m a month.
